record.paper_title: Electromagnetic probes in heavy-ion collisions: progress and open questions
record.original_question: How can photon and dilepton observables be used at lower collision energies, such as those in the RHIC beam energy scan, HADES, and future FAIR experiments, to understand the early stage of heavy-ion collisions and the temperature- and baryon-chemical-potential dependence of the equation of state and transport coefficients, when the quark-gluon-plasma phase is shorter relative to the complex early stage and hard-process calculations are more difficult because the center-of-mass energy is lower?

evidence.quote: The discussion of all the different sources of photons and dileptons presented above is not only relevant for high-energy nuclear collisions (LHC and top RHIC collision energies), but also for lower energy collisions studied in the beam energy scan at RHIC, as well as the HADES and future FAIR experiment at GSI.
Many of the challenges discussed above are amplified in lower collision energies. In particular, the quark-gluon plasma phase is shorter relative to the complex early stage of the collisions.
Calculations of the contribution of hard processes (Section 3) is also more difficult due to the lower center-of-mass energies.
Calculations of photons using a hydrodynamic-based model are reported in Ref. [35]; they show the potential of photons to help understand the early stage of the collisions.
More generally, photons and dileptons can help better understand the transition to and from the hydrodynamics regime, which is particularly important at lower collision energies.
Photons and dileptons further provide a valuable tool to study the temperature and baryon chemical potential dependence of the equation of state and transport coefficients.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider relativistic heavy-ion collisions at center-of-mass energies per nucleon pair in the range relevant to the RHIC beam energy scan and to the HADES and FAIR fixed-target programs (roughly a few GeV up to a few tens of GeV), where the quark–gluon plasma (QGP) phase, if formed, occupies a small fraction of the total space-time evolution relative to a prolonged and complex pre-equilibrium stage and an extended hadronic phase, and where perturbative hard-process calculations are unreliable because of the modest center-of-mass energy. The system is modeled by a multistage description (initial state, pre-equilibrium, viscous relativistic hydrodynamics with an equation of state p(T,μ_B) and transport coefficients such as shear viscosity η/s(T,μ_B) and bulk viscosity ζ/s(T,μ_B) depending on temperature T and baryon chemical potential μ_B, followed by hadronic transport), in which thermal photons and dileptons are emitted at all stages with rates determined by the in-medium electromagnetic spectral function ρ_EM(ω,k;T,μ_B).

Formulate a quantitative framework that determines:
(a) which inclusive and differential photon and dilepton observables (e.g., transverse-momentum spectra, invariant-mass spectra dN/dM, elliptic and triangular flow coefficients v_n(p_T) and v_n(M), polarization observables) carry distinguishable sensitivity to the early, pre-equilibrium stage of the collision as opposed to the hydrodynamic and hadronic stages;
(b) how these observables constrain the (T, μ_B) dependence of the equation of state and of the transport coefficients η/s(T,μ_B) and ζ/s(T,μ_B) in the finite-μ_B regime accessed at lower collision energies; and
(c) how to handle the diminished reliability of hard-process (prompt photon, Drell–Yan) baselines at these energies within such a framework.

Specifically, identify or construct photon/dilepton observables (or combinations thereof) whose theoretical predictions, computed within a hydrodynamic-based multistage model with prescribed ρ_EM, are demonstrably more sensitive to the early-stage dynamics and to the finite-μ_B equation of state and transport coefficients than to uncertainties in the hadronic-phase emission and the missing hard-process contribution.
artifact.status_search_result: This is an active research direction in relativistic heavy-ion phenomenology. Photon and dilepton measurements in the RHIC beam energy scan, HADES, and the upcoming CBM/FAIR program are still being developed and analyzed; theoretical frameworks for extracting the finite-μ_B equation of state and transport coefficients from electromagnetic observables remain under active development with no settled, fully quantitative answer.

status_evidence.title: Electromagnetic probes in heavy-ion collisions: progress and open questions
status_evidence.snippet: Review identifies open questions concerning photon and dilepton observables at lower collision energies (BES, HADES, FAIR) and their use to constrain the early stage and the (T, μ_B)-dependent equation of state and transport coefficients.
status_evidence.claim: The question is presented as an open research direction in the field.
